correctness.rationale: The proof excludes all \(\alpha>1/2\) by explicit permanently missing integers and proves \(2^{-k}\) complete for every integer \(k\ge1\) by binary expansion. It derives the exact identity \(H_n(\alpha)=1+\alpha(n-3)-\sum_{j=1}^n\{\alpha(2^j+1)\}+\{\alpha(2^{n+1}+1)\}\). Orthogonality of lacunary exponentials gives \(\int_0^1|T_N|^2=1/N\); Borel--Cantelli on square indices, interpolation, Weyl, and translation show the fractional-part average tends to \(1/2\) almost everywhere. Thus \(H_n/n\to\alpha-1/2\) and the permanently omitted interval has length \((1/2-\alpha)n+o(n)\). Exact rational checks passed; finite tests are not used as proofs of the infinite assertions.

value.rationale: The claim directly addresses the critical boundary between Ma--Chen\'s positive-measure theorem for uniform \(\gamma<2\) and Wu--Ma\'s existence theorem when ratios may reach two. The natural perturbation \(s_n=2^n+1\) satisfies the strictly sharper pointwise inequality \(s_{n+1}<2s_n\) yet its successful scaling set is null and infinite. The explicit almost-everywhere linear missing-interval asymptotic explains the mechanism quantitatively. This is a motivated sharp boundary example, not an arbitrary finite computation.
